title: Registration announced; original nine-member board
summary: Report published 2 February 2023 says the AOA had been registered and lists an initial nine-member board. This is a publication date, not a verified registration date.

title: Association website: registration number and board
summary: Displays GBN/10037/2022-2023 and a board headed by Vinod Negi, labelled 2024-25. The live fetch returned an empty body; indexed content is not reliable proof of the present board. No original registration certificate was obtained.

title: AOA notice: first GBM and handover roadmap
summary: Notice dated 3 April calls a 7 April 2024 GBM. Agenda covers former-AOA/EC handover and a builder-services roadmap. Notice proves an agenda was issued, not that a transfer was completed.

title: AOA notice: builder/GNIDA CAM handover and MOU
summary: 17 July notice invites residents to a 21 July 2024 meeting about ongoing builder/GNIDA discussions, CAM handover, MOU and further action. The signed MOU and meeting minutes are absent.

title: AOA notice: MOU compliance and NPCL multipoint
summary: 14 December notice calls a 22 December 2024 GBM on infrastructure, NPCL multipoint and compliance with the Panchsheel Buildtech MOU. It establishes these issues were on the agenda by 2024.

title: 1 August 2025 election judgment: 17915 with 19634
summary: Common judgment quashed the 15 May 2025 Deputy Registrar order and remitted the matter to the Prescribed Authority. Judicial text was read; official signed PDF not obtained. Hindi quotation in the mirror is corrupted.

title: 13 May 2026 judgment plus 20 May correction
summary: Six-page court order sheet from the official High Court portal; includes the five-page decision and one-page date correction. Corrected dates are used in this archive. Neutral citation visible on the original: 2026:AHC:110600. Key PDF pages: 5 (directions), 6 (correction).

title: Official case status: Writ-C 18764/2026
summary: Captured 3 November 2026. Filed 7 May, registered 8 May; disposed 13 May. Correction IA filed 18 May and disposed 20 May. A stay IA still marked pending is a database field, not proof of operative relief.

title: Official current case status: Writ-C 45508/2026
summary: Filed 29 October; registered 3 November 2026. Pending, Newly Fresh. No first/next hearing date shown and portal says Order/Judgement Not Found. Full petition and interim prayers remain unavailable.

title: Deputy Registrar reportedly halted proposed March election
summary: 23 February 2026 reporting says a 1 March election was stopped while the earlier election dispute remained before SDM Dadri. It records residents challenging the proposed process. Original administrative order is missing.

title: News interpretation of May High Court decision
summary: 15 May report described elections within one month and quoted AOA assurances. The actual judgment has a two-stage timetable: reference decision first, election within one month thereafter. Use the judgment for the operative directions.

title: 30 September SDM decision reported on 6 October
summary: Reports dismissal for lack of sufficient one-quarter membership support and treatment of the 22 March 2025 election as valid. Article discusses 1,211 eligible voters, about 303 needed, and lists of 355, 174 and 85 signatures. It names the deciding officer as SDM Dadri Abhinendra Singh and says he directed the Deputy Registrar, Ghaziabad to take further action; no case number is given. Original order and lists are missing.

title: October election-officer process reported
summary: 17 October report says an officer nominated by Deputy Registrar issued directions on 15 October requiring AOA documents by 19 October. Also reports resident demands for financial transparency and facility improvements. Original notice is missing.

title: Approved GH-08A site plan
summary: Approved site plan for Plot GH-08A, Sector-1 (30,000 sq m / 7.41 acres), revised sanction stamped May 2014. Towers T1-T7 are stilt + 14 floors (84 flats each), T8 and T9 stilt + 24 (144 and 96 flats), T10 and T11 stilt + 20 (160 each), T12 stilt + 21 with community area (164). That is 988 flats at 2.75 FAR plus 324 purchasable-FAR flats = 1,312. It also records 1,132 car and 650 two-wheeler spaces (minimum 1,003 cars), projected population 5,904, ground coverage 31.27%, 10,326 sq m green area, a commercial block, three entries from service roads and 6 m fire-tender roads.

title: Registered sublease exemplar: rights and handover clauses
summary: A registered sublease publicly filed on UP RERA for one Phase-1 flat. Its schedule grants use of one covered car space; clause 30 says parking and certain facilities will not be handed to the association; clause 40 recognises applicable law. Not reproduced or linked here because it carries a buyer's personal details. Contract wording is not a ruling on enforceability.

title: Allotment exemplar: FOC parking versus general clause
summary: Allotment exemplar publicly filed on UP RERA. Page 3 itemises one covered parking FOC; page 9 clause 30 describes parking on request/payment, first-come-first-served and a separate agreement. Not reproduced here because it carries a buyer's personal details. Individual promises need reconciliation with boilerplate.

title: GNIDA Tower-10 occupancy/completion certificate
summary: Visually reviewed certificate dated 31 October 2018 concerns Tower-10, 160 units. Conditions include prior authority permission for changes and parking only in designated plan areas; it is not a whole-society occupancy certificate.

title: January 2024 water crisis / builder-control context
summary: 28 January report describes supply disruption, residents alleging builder water dues of about Rs 2 crore and an ad hoc AOA while builder remained in control. The maintenance representative disputed the dues and shortage account. No audited account or water-demand order was obtained.

title: Water dispute, complaint and police intervention
summary: 1 July 2024 reporting describes a resident assault complaint arising from a 23 June pump-room dispute, a police reconciliation meeting and warnings over hostile WhatsApp messages. This is not a conviction; original complaint, FIR status and police notice are not in hand.

title: AOA response to criticism during water crisis
summary: Reports Anjali Negi defending AOA response to June water problems, pump replacement/tankers and approaches to GNIDA/MP. It records supportive residents too. Publication date was not independently resolved; do not infer a judicial finding from the headline.

title: Gate-2 boom-barrier disagreement
summary: 27 August 2024 article describes gate access restrictions reversed after police intervention. Its title names Hynish but body says Panchsheel Heights; attribution needs corroboration. Its accusatory headline is not adopted.

title: Water-quality notices in February 2025
summary: Reports GNIDA notices to Hynish and Arihant Arden. The Rs 5 lakh fine described in the headline was imposed on Ecovillage-1, not Hynish. Hynish-specific notice and water-test results are missing.

title: Basement-market flooding and maintenance concerns
summary: 14 August 2025 report describes repeated basement-market flooding and trader losses at Hynish, with commercial area described as AOA-maintained. Loss amounts and responsibility were not established by an adjudication in the materials obtained.

title: Shopkeeper complaint alleging duplicate maintenance charges
summary: 19 August 2025 poster alleges maintenance deductions through a prepaid meter plus separate invoices. This website post is not a consumer-court judgment or verified case filing. AOA response and reconciled ledger were not obtained.

title: Multipoint implementation dispute in late October
summary: 2 November 2026 report says residents alleged obstruction when NPCL arrived after an asserted 22 October notice scheduling 28 October work. The actual NPCL notice, site report and AOA response are missing; obstruction and motive remain allegations.

title: Cheque-dispute proceeding: Anjali Negi and two others
summary: 21 April 2026 order in BNSS 8843/2026 concerns challenge to summons in Complaint 380/2025 (Panchsheel Buildtech v Panchsheel Hynish Apartment and others), Section 138 NI Act. It provides a compromise/compounding route and temporary protection; no acquittal, final settlement or parking relief is established.

title: Tower-12 registry litigation: 29 owners
summary: 9 April 2026 reporting describes a 90-day registry direction for 29 petitioning Tower-12 owners, funded by them. The case is Writ-C 13589/2026; as quoted by the Authority (S79) the order directed a decision on a representation, not registry. This is a separate ownership matter, not proof of an AOA election or parking outcome.

title: UP Apartment Act 2010: statutory copy
summary: Reference copy of the Act for framework and comparison. This archive does not certify that the copy includes every later amendment or decide the enforceability of a particular contract.

title: Environmental recovery reporting includes Hynish
summary: June 2026 report lists Hynish among societies in STP recovery action. The overall figures relate to 167 societies; no Hynish-specific liability amount, addressee or final recovery status was verified. Original demand/recovery certificate is required.

title: Mid-2025 report: AOA declared time-expired; supply officer as election officer
summary: Page metadata dates it 29 June 2025. Says the term ended 15 March 2025, the Deputy Registrar declared the AOA time-expired, the District Supply Officer was named election officer, and residents wrote to the DM for support and an ad hoc arrangement. No order date or reference is given. Fits the period after the 15 May 2025 DR order but is not confirmed by an original order.

title: February 2026 complaint to DM about AOA functioning
summary: 17 February 2026 report says the executive had not received formal Deputy Registrar recognition, the matter was before SDM Dadri, and residents alleged large collections for renovation and arbitrary GBM attempts. A resident sought an impartial DM inquiry. AOA office-bearers called all allegations baseless. No amounts or orders given.

title: Late-October multipoint dispute: notice addressed to builder and AOA
summary: 30 October 2026 report says NPCL had already surveyed the society, its 22 October notice went to both the builder and the AOA, and the 28 October team returned amid AOA opposition. Residents also allege single-point recharges were tied to other dues. AOA account not included; no UPERC direction or police record mentioned.

title: NPCL post on Hynish multipoint consent (search-result lead)
summary: Search-result text attributes to NPCL a post saying most Hynish respondents opted for multipoint, with an AOA-NPCL meeting on 20 May 2024 before a survey. The post itself could not be opened (X refused access), so wording, date and response counts are unverified.

title: UPERC single-point to multipoint conversion framework
summary: 2018 reporting on a UPERC suo motu Supply Code amendment directing conversion of single-point connections, with societies exempt only where 51% choose single-point. Later coverage (Outlook Business) records UPERC criticising discoms for delay. Coverage is 2018-2022; the current regulation text and any NPCL-specific order were not obtained.

title: NGT groundwater case names Panchsheel Hynish as respondent
summary: OA 392/2022, Prasoon Pant v Union of India: 5 July 2022 order lists Hynish among respondent builders accused of illegal groundwater extraction and directs a CPCB/UPPCB/DM joint committee report. No Hynish-specific finding or compensation appears in that order. Later UPPCB reports are hosted on greentribunal.gov.in but could not be opened (certificate error).

title: GSTAT anti-profiteering order covering Hynish Tower-10
kind: Legal news report of tribunal order
summary: NAPA/59/PB/2025, DGAP v Panchsheel Buildtech, GSTAT Delhi, order reported as 20 February (2026). For Hynish Tower-10: 161 eligible buyers, Rs 29,68,382 profiteered. Builder to pass benefit with interest; 10% penalty if repayment delayed beyond 20 March 2026; compliance report within two months. Signed order and compliance not obtained.

title: AOA formation reported, with president's statement
summary: 3 February 2023 CitySpidey report (read via Wayback; live site unreachable). The first president said residents registered the association on 31 January 2023, renamed it Panchsheel Hynish Flat Owners Association, and that the nine members were chosen unanimously and announced at a general meeting.

title: March 2024 election: two panels, 7-2 result
summary: 21 March 2024 Tricity Today report (read via Wayback). Election held 16 March 2024 under an administration-appointed election officer; two panels contested, one won 7 of 9 seats. Office-bearers named: Anjali Negi (president), Amrendra Pratap Singh (vice-president), Vijay Rastogi (secretary), Himanshu Gautam (treasurer). Winners said getting handover from the builder was the main goal.

title: AOA delegation meets the MP during water shortage
summary: 26 June 2024. AOA office-bearers, a coordination committee and 40-50 residents met MP Dr Mahesh Sharma, who reportedly spoke to Authority officials and the builder and asked for a quick fix. The headline doubts follow-through.

title: Memorandum demanding the 2025-26 election
summary: 30 January 2025. Two AOA members handed the president a residents' memorandum asking for the 2025-26 election process and a GBM to form an election committee. No AOA response reported.

title: Deputy Registrar cancels February 2025 GBM and committee
summary: 8 March 2025. Report says residents complained the election committee formed at the 16 February 2025 GBM was one-sided; after hearing both sides on 28 February the Deputy Registrar cancelled that GBM and declared the committee invalid, so the planned 9 March election did not go ahead. Original order not obtained; no AOA response in the article.

title: Deputy Registrar orders fresh election within a month
summary: 18 May 2025. Reports a Deputy Registrar order for a fresh election within one month with the District Backward Class Welfare Officer as election officer, and that the time-expired AOA was limited to essential expenses. The account comes through a resident; a June 2025 report names a different officer (S33). The High Court quashed the 15 May 2025 DR order on 1 August 2025.

title: DR stays proposed March 2026 election
summary: 23 February 2026. After a complaint to the DM's office, the Deputy Registrar stayed the AOA election because the earlier election dispute was pending before SDM Dadri. Residents said the AOA announced a schedule unilaterally; the paper says the AOA president did not answer calls.

title: Handover to AOA reported on 6 September 2024
summary: Last updated 24 September 2024. Residents say the society was handed over to the AOA with the builder on 6 September 2024 without settling advance maintenance and IFMS, that maintenance rose 45%, and that the STP and pumps were not working. No AOA or builder response included; the handover document itself is not public. AOA records give 7 September 2024 (S89).

title: AOA website noticeboard (archived snapshot)
summary: 2 March 2026 Wayback snapshot of phaoa.in (live page returns empty). Shows GBN/10037/2022-2023, Plot GH-08A, office at T2-601, and notices for meetings on 12 March, 11 May, 13 July and 24 August 2025, plus a call for civil repair and painting proposals.

title: Power-cut protests; NPCL cites damaged transformer
summary: 27 May 2024. Residents protested long outages. NPCL said a transformer inside the society was damaged and that a notice had been served on the society.

title: Water-queue video from Hynish draws coverage
summary: 23 June 2024. A viral video showed residents queueing for water during the summer shortage.

title: Residents protest over unopened swimming pool
summary: 13 May 2024 (Apartment Times covered the same protest on 12 May). Residents said the pool was built about four years earlier but never started by the builder, and questioned maintenance spending. No builder response.

title: Lift drop reported in Tower 3
summary: 7 December 2024 roundup. Unnamed residents said a Tower-3 lift fell from the 3rd floor to the ground floor; the passenger was not injured. No date or official finding given.

title: Basement market waterlogged after rain
summary: 12 August 2025, spelled "Panchsheel Highness". Rain flooded the basement shops; management pumped water out; residents said it keeps recurring.

title: Green-belt counters and fire-lane parking dispute
summary: 26 October 2026, spelled "Highness" (matched by location and quoted resident; medium confidence). Residents objected to food counters in the market green belt and parking in the 6 m fire-tender lane; police calmed the situation; residents sought a joint district/GNIDA/fire inspection.

title: Resident video: failed prepaid meter and disconnection threat
summary: 2 November 2026, spelled "Highness". A resident says several prepaid meters failed within months, his was switched to temporary postpaid, and he was asked to buy a new meter rather than get a warranty replacement, with a disconnection threat; police attended. No AOA or NPCL response.

title: Registry still pending a month after High Court order
summary: 12 May 2026. About 300 families in two towers still awaited registry. Describes the 9 April order as directing the Authority to examine and decide within three months, and says residents reported no action by the Authority or builder.

title: Tower-12 registry order: 29 petitioners, 90 days
summary: 11 April 2026 Navbharat Times. Allahabad High Court directed completion of the sub-lease registry for 29 petitioning Tower-12 owners within 90 days; Tower 12 has 150+ owners and relief covers only petitioners. Describes the order differently from S56; the signed order is needed. The order as quoted by the Authority (S79) directed a decision within three months, not registry.

title: UP RERA phase data (aggregator copy)
summary: Phase 1 UPRERAPRJ8533 (T8-T9): start 8 Aug 2014, completion 8 May 2018. Phase 2 UPRERAPRJ8538 (T10-T11): 1 Oct 2015 to 1 Oct 2019. Phase 3 UPRERAPRJ8545 (T12): 2 Jul 2016 to 1 Jan 2021. All shown Completed on plot GH08A. The official up-rera.in portal could not be opened to confirm.

title: Builder's project page
summary: Status "Delivered", 12 towers, 1,305 units, RERA UPRERAPRJ8533, promoter UPRERAPRM6558. Gives no possession or certificate dates. Unit count differs from the approved plan (1,312).

title: Property listing: phases and land area
summary: Lists 12 towers, 1,312 units, 7.41 acres, Phase-1 launch 8 Aug 2014, Phase 2 Oct 2015, Phase 3 Jul 2016, and "ready to move since Jan 2021". Marketing listing; dates contradict each other in places.

title: Property listing: plot, sizes and launch prices
summary: Gives "Plot No. GH-08, Sector 1", launch Aug 2014, possession May 2018, 1,312 units, up to 24 floors, 7.41 acres, flats 755-1,550 sq ft, listed prices Rs 31.71-65.10 lakh (sold out). Marketing listing.

title: Property listing: address and nearby places
summary: Gives Sector 1, Bisrakh Jalalpur 201318, 12 towers, 1,312 units, 7.00 acres, possession January 2021; nearby Sarvottam International School (2.2 km), Noida Sector-101 metro (6.9 km), Gaur City Mall (7.1 km). Marketing listing.

title: 2016 builder press release
summary: 15 January 2016. Markets 2 and 3 BHK homes at a base price of Rs 3,724 per sq ft, with a 60 m front road, 24 m side road, club, gym and rainwater harvesting. Promotional text, not a verified record.

title: 2019 snapshot: 700 families, 10 towers occupied
summary: 30 August 2019. Says over 700 families lived in Hynish, with 10 towers occupied and 2 under construction. The rest concerns lift complaints.

title: Supreme Court upholds Shahberi acquisition quashing
summary: 6 July 2011. Supreme Court upheld quashing of about 156 ha acquisition in Shahberi, Greater Noida West, and fined the Authority Rs 10 lakh. Area-wide; Hynish not named.

title: High Court quashes Patwari acquisition
summary: July 2011. Allahabad High Court quashed acquisition of about 589 ha in Patwari and Dewla, where buyers had booked homes. Area-wide; Hynish not named.

title: Builders allowed to resume after Master Plan 2021 approval
summary: 28 August 2012. After NCR Planning Board approval of Master Plan 2021, the Authority let Noida Extension builders resume work after about ten months; the halt was treated as a zero period. Panchsheel not named.

title: Supreme Court upholds Greater Noida acquisitions
summary: May 2015. Supreme Court upheld the High Court approach of extra compensation (about 64%) and developed land for farmers; reported as removing the obstruction to construction. Area-wide.

title: Greater Noida West metro link approved by PIB
summary: 23 July 2026. Public Investment Board approved an 8.4 km elevated line from Noida Sector 61 to Greater Noida West Sector 4 (Gaur Chowk), about Rs 2,000 crore, pending Union Cabinet approval.

title: NPCL multipoint progress across Greater Noida
summary: 7 April 2026. NPCL says 91 societies now have individual connections (23 converted from single-point, 68 new); notices went to 130+ societies, some refused; UPERC order requires conversion. Hynish not named.

title: UP Electricity Supply Code amendments index
summary: UPPCL page (updated 20 November 2025) listing the 13th Amendment to the Supply Code 2005 on single-point and multipoint connections in multi-storey buildings and the UPERC order of 17 May 2019. The amendment text itself was not machine-readable.

title: Commentary: AOA board term under UP Apartment Act
summary: 10 January 2025. Explains the model bye-laws' one-year board term and their inconsistencies, and reports an Allahabad High Court ruling (Windsor Park RWA, Writ-C 12380/2023) that all board posts go to annual election. Secondary source, not the bye-law text.

title: GNIDA allotment of the larger GH-08 plot
summary: Greater Noida Authority letter No. Builders/2010/1414 dated 19 March 2010 allots Group Housing Plot GH-08, Sector-01 (204,000 sq m) to a consortium led by Supertech Ltd with Panchsheel Buildtech as a member, at Rs 10,044 per sq m, with premium payable in half-yearly instalments to 2018 and beyond. Read from the scanned copy filed with RERA.

title: Lease deed for sub-plot GH-08A
summary: Lease deed for Plot GH-08A, Sector-01 in favour of Panchsheel Buildtech, registered at Gautam Budh Nagar as document 17410 of 2010 (receipt dated 6 July 2010). Its endorsement records an agreement to lease executed 1 April 2010. Read from the scanned copy filed with RERA.

title: GNIDA revised building-plan sanction for GH-08A
summary: Letter dated 21 May 2014 grants revised sanction of the building plan on Plot GH-08A, Sector-01, valid five years, conditional on environment and groundwater NOCs. Conditions include gates opening only to the service road, no parking on the road, basement ventilation, and compliance with the UP Apartment Act 2010.

title: "Hynish Specifications" sheet
summary: Specification sheet signed 13 January 2018: earthquake-resistant RCC frame, vitrified-tile floors, granite kitchen platform, 2 or 3 high-speed lifts per tower, ISI copper wiring, intercom and DTH provision.

title: Location: Google Maps listing
summary: Google Maps lists "Panchsheel Hynish" at plus code HCHQ+J5, Sector 1, Bisrakh Jalalpur, Greater Noida 201318, near Supertech Ecovillage-1 and Nirala Greenshire Road (about 28.5791 N, 77.4379 E). Map pins are approximate.

title: High Court judgment of 1 August 2025: official signed PDF
kind: Primary court document · copy circulated to members
summary: Digitally signed judgment (2025:AHC:129355, Court No. 32) in Writ-C 17915/2025 with 19634/2025; not a certified copy. Its Hindi passages are legible. It quotes the Deputy Registrar order of 15 May 2025, which discarded the 22 March 2025 election under Section 25(2) because the election committee was formed by show of hands and share certificates were issued selectively, barred policy decisions, and named the District Backward Class Welfare Officer as election officer. The Court found only procedural objections, which belong to the Prescribed Authority under Section 25(1), set the order aside and remitted the matter.

title: Greater Noida Authority order of 15 July 2026 on the Tower-11/12 sub-lease representation
summary: Order of the Authority's ACEO (Builders) under Allahabad High Court Writ-C 13589/2026, Sourabh Thukral and 28 others v. State of U.P. and 3 others. It quotes the High Court order of 9 April 2026: counsel confined the prayer to a decision on the home-buyers' 12 February 2026 representation, and the writ was disposed of without any view on the merits, the representation to be decided preferably within three months of the certified copy. After a hearing on 2 June 2026 the Authority records a part temporary occupancy certificate for 1,029 units/shops with 1,015 sub-leases executed, lease rent of Rs 92,97,055 due, and no completion certificate for Towers 11 and 12. It directs the builder to deposit the lease rent and, within three months, obtain completion for Towers 11 and 12 and execute sub-leases for their home-buyers. Letter number and day are handwritten. Not reproduced here because it names individual home-buyers.

title: Deed of Declaration (Form A), 3 December 2015
kind: Statutory declaration (scanned) · copy circulated to members
summary: Form A declaration under the UP Apartment Act by Panchsheel Buildtech for "Plot No GH-08, Sector-1, 30,000 sq m", leasehold for 99 years under a lease deed of 6 July 2010. Annex B lists 12 towers and 1,312 apartments (84 each in T1-T7, then 144, 96, 160, 160 and 164). Annex D lists a single 7,513 sq m basement (STP, parking, ramp, panels, tank), lawns 875 sq m, play area 250, pool 213, basketball 428, two badminton courts, a 960 sq m club, and 2 lifts per tower in T1-T7 and 3 in T8-T12; it states "No parking provided in common area & Facilities" and gives the allotted area as 209,557 sq m, of which 30,000 sq m is Panchsheel's. Annexures E and F (limited common and independent areas), several original pages and any registration endorsement are not in this copy; area totals differ between clause FOURTH and Annex C.

title: Authority meeting minutes no. 215 (27 May 2024)
kind: Official minutes · copy circulated to members
summary: Minutes of a 21 May 2024 meeting chaired by the Authority's ACEO (Builders) with the builder and AOA office-bearers. The society's electricity connection was still in the builder's name; the builder said it would transfer it if the AOA refunded the NPCL security deposit, and the AOA agreed. The AOA asked for multipoint supply. A draft handover agreement was being prepared, and handover of the connection and maintenance was directed by 15 July 2024.

title: Authority minutes no. 234 of the 16 July 2024 meeting, with AOA letter of 18 July 2024
summary: Minutes issued 25 July 2024 (day handwritten) of an Authority-builder-AOA meeting: the builder's MD said signing of the builder-AOA MOU was "in progress"; the AOA said MOU annexure points were unresolved; power, DG, STP, fire and lift issues were raised. The attached AOA letter of 18 July 2024 asked for a handover order before 1 August 2024 and cited an NPCL survey recommending three 1,500 kVA transformers. Not reproduced here because the attachment carries personal phone numbers and e-mail addresses.

title: Deputy Registrar letter 3194 of 15 February 2025
summary: Forwarding a residents' complaint of 11 February 2025, the Deputy Registrar told the AOA to hold its election under the UP Apartment Act 2010 and model bye-laws 2011. The complaint said the Deed of Declaration had not been amended; the letter quotes the joint-owner rule (only the first-named owner votes) and warns that an election against the rules would be void. Not reproduced here because its copy list carries residents' flat numbers.

title: District Supply Officer (election officer) letter 638 of 1 July 2025
kind: Official letter · copy circulated to members
summary: The District Supply Officer, Gautam Buddh Nagar, nominated election officer by letter 600 of 20 June 2025, told the AOA to supply the Deed of Declaration, membership/voter list, registered bye-laws and an estimated election cost of Rs 2,56,000 by 5 July 2025 for an election within one month, warning of action under the UP Apartment Act 2010. Copied to the DM and the Deputy Registrar.

title: Deputy Registrar order 3169 of 31 December 2025
summary: Recalls DR letter 6021 of 25 August 2025, which referred the election dispute to the Prescribed Authority (SDM Dadri) under Section 25(1). On a complaint of 24 December 2025 that GBMs were being called while the reference was pending, it says that AGBMs not held according to the rules would be void. It does not itself declare particular meetings void. Not reproduced here because its copy list carries a resident's flat number.

title: NPCL final notice of 17 July 2020 on multipoint
kind: Utility notice · copy circulated to members
summary: NPCL notice to the builder, the society and residents, after its letter of 21 August 2018 on the 13th Amendment to the Supply Code and reminders in 2020. Under the UPERC orders of 17 May 2019 and 2 March 2020, multipoint supply was presumed unless the association resolved by majority to keep single point; the society had 30 days or would be deemed to have opted for multipoint.

title: NPCL notice 144 of 15 September 2026
kind: Utility notice · copy circulated to members
summary: Addressed to the builder's MD and the AOA President/Secretary, copied to UPERC, the ADM, the DCP and residents via the notice board. Requires compliance within 15 days with the UPERC tariff order of 10 October 2024 for single-point bulk consumers: half-yearly reports of amounts collected from residents against amounts paid to NPCL, and a CA audit uploaded to NPCL's portal. Penalties of Rs 5,000, 10,000 and 15,000 for the first three defaults; otherwise NPCL would begin withdrawing single point and converting to multipoint at the cost of "you / residents". One sentence is cut at the page break.

title: NPCL final notice 156 of 22 October 2026
kind: Utility notice · copy circulated to members
summary: Addressed to the builder's MD and, by name, AOA President Vinod Negi and Secretary Vijay Rastogi; copied to the DM/ADM, DCP and UPERC. NPCL says that after seeking police help on 14 October, its team, police and service provider visited on 15 October 2026, met resistance from about 200 residents insisting on a fresh survey, and halted on police advice. It demands access within 24 hours and a nominated society representative, says the team will come again on 28 October, refuses a re-survey and warns of disconnection. Basis given: "three defaults" under the tariff order and the 13th Amendment, and resident complaints that electricity charges were adjusted into CAM and dues recovered through recharges. It does not say the AOA organised the opposition.

title: AOA records giving the handover date
kind: Association records circulated to members · seen, not reproduced
summary: Three AOA minutes (22 December 2024, 24 August 2025, 17 February 2026) say the AOA took over maintenance from the builder on 7 September 2024; the AOA events deck and its annual "Hynish Day" on 7 September use the same date, and an AOA water circular gives "September 2024". The handover agreement and inventory themselves are not in these records. Not reproduced here because they are members-only minutes.

title: Community: Hynish Day, cricket league and AOA events deck
kind: Community notices circulated to members · seen, not reproduced
summary: "Hynish Day" on 7 September marks the 2024 handover; a resident cricket league reached Season 4 in mid-2025 (52 players, 4 captains); an AOA deck shows festivals, national-day events, health and children's camps, plantation and cleanliness drives. Self-published by organisers: shows that events were held, not attendance. Not reproduced here because they carry residents' names and photographs.
